sections.title: The Structure of Enterprise Commerce has Changed.
sections.content:
Enterprise commerce leadersare nolongersolving forbasicfunctionality. They are managing integration debt, cross-borderlogistics, fragmented data, rising acquisition costs, and increasing margin pressure – all areas that leaders can’t rely on AI to manage on its own.

Enterprise brands today face:

• HybridB2BandB2Coperations • Marketplace pressure from Amazon and 3P sellers • Global inventory coordination • Escalating shipping and return costs • 70% cart abandonment rates • Security and fraud exposure • The dilemma between sophistication and total cost of ownership

sections.title: The Salesforce Model requires:
sections.content:
From Monolithic Fortress to Modular Skyscraper

Legacy commerce systems were designed like rigid fortresses: interconnected and difficult to remodel. Updating a single component often meant disturbing the entire structure. Today’s enterprise brands need a different approach to commerce: An infrastructure blueprint that supports change without destabilizing operations, like building a modern skyscraper from modular components that rest within a stable structural core.

So, which architectural model best supports scale and complexity without increasing structural friction?

This analysis compares VTEX and Salesforce against core enterprise pain points to determine which infrastructure model provides the winning blueprint for modern enterprise commerce.

Two Blueprints. Two Architectural Models.

Commerce (Agentforce)

A CRM-centered ecosystem extending into commerce through multiple clouds. Its strength lies in deep Acommerce-native, multi-tenant SaaS customer data integration platform with builtacross marketing, service, inmarketplace, and sales functions, enabling enterprises to order management, connect commerce activity and unified B2B/B2C with broader customer capabilities under a lifecycle management. single infrastructure layer.

The distinction is structural:

Salesforce prioritizes CRM-driven customer intelligence and crossdepartment workflows. VTEX prioritizes unified commerce infrastructure designed to run complex operations at scale.

Laying the Foundation of Operational Infrastructure

While highly capable, this layered construction can introduce added complexity and coordination across systems. Enterprise brands face disconnected systems, middleware reliance, and “app overload,” which increases risk and slows innovation.
